SMTO-EXE-0018 — That recovery choice isn't available right now

GUID: 6f9b42fb-4cda-4cff-907e-c511aae31c96
Slug: resource-recovery-action-not-eligible
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • The choice you made for the blocking job isn't allowed in its current state, for example because it can't safely be ended yet. Nothing was done, and your blocked command still hasn't started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment for the recovery card in the task to refresh; SMTO reloads it after this message. The refreshed card only enables the choices that are allowed right now.
  2. Select a button on the card that isn't greyed out, such as Wait until the job state changes. Choices that aren't allowed are turned off; an available one lets the task move on.
  3. If no choice is available, let the other job finish, or select Stop to end this task. When the blocking job ends, SMTO continues on its own; stopping ends the wait if you no longer need the task.

What success looks like

  • Your choice is accepted and the card shows Waiting for the job state to change…, or the task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't end the blocking job some other way while the card says that isn't allowed; it may still be doing work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The resource reconciliation route rejected the action because it is not among the currently enabled actions for the blocker (for example reset is not enabled and no saved reset decision exists to continue).

What this means

  • The reset route found no enabled reset action in the current decision and no retained reset decision that it could continue. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The reset route found no enabled reset action in the current decision and no retained reset decision that it could continue.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh current actions and inspect any existing reset decision before assuming that a new reset is permitted.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the run's resource_reconciliation_request and submit only an action listed as enabled in its actions (or accept / stop_blocker / request_override when their eligibility conditions hold). For reset, the decision must expose an enabled reset action or the prerequisite must already carry a reset_decision.
  • Refresh recovery state and select a currently supported action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported recovery flow offers reset for the current state or another eligible action settles the blocker.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
